headline: Engadget has compared Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, the two always-on AI agents that keep working in the cloud after a user leaves, and finds the biggest gaps in price, permissions and where they are offered.
score_reason: Kept at 4: the comparison and Engadget's own hands-on findings are new on 12 Oct 2026, read in full; the launches it compares are older and already carried, so it is not raised.
importance_line: People choosing a paid always-on assistant face about $100 a month for OpenAI's Dots against a free capped start and $20 for Muse's first paid tier, and either one needs access to email, calendar and files, but this is one outlet's comparison, both firms say their agents can make mistakes, and Muse is limited to the US and Canada.
summary: Engadget reports in a side-by-side comparison that Meta's Muse, released on 8 Sep 2026, and OpenAI's Dots, launched about three weeks later and carried in our 30 Sep 2026 edition, both keep working after the user leaves and run their own cloud computer, but Muse has a free tier with a usage cap and paid tiers at $20 and $100 a month, while the cheapest individual route to Dots is OpenAI's $100-a-month Pro 100 plan. Muse is available only in the US and Canada, Dots are not yet offered to Pro users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland or the UK, and Engadget found Muse's setting that lets Meta use interactions to improve its AI models switched on by default.
notes: Read Engadget in full. The comparison is new reporting, but the launches it compares are older (Muse 8 Sep 2026; Dots at OpenAI DevDay, 29 Sep 2026, carried in our 30 Sep edition); QA may judge it a follow-up of that launch. Prices, permissions and availability are as stated by Engadget and the companies.
